description:
North star: compile work proportional to input; things nothing uses create no work or artifacts.

Fact (HEAD 5ea6a5830, after fz-xxd.11): an extern no caller reaches runs 4 jobs: ExpandFunctionSource, DefineFunction, DeriveStaticCallees, DeriveInputDemand. It gets no contract, lowering, entry dispatch or executable. 00420 has 19 of them (76 jobs). Smallest case: `def main(), do: 1 + 2` touches fz_op_add_if and fz_op_add_ff through the unselected clauses of Kernel.+/2 (lib/kernel.fz:291-293).

Cause: two whole-body walks with no clause-reachability filter:
- DeriveStaticCallees(+) -> body_static_callees -> static_edges over every clause (keying.rs:126, 1119-1138). DeriveCallGraphComponent's collect_static_graph (keying.rs:1068-1091) then waits on StaticCallees of each callee, and the blocked-waiter expansion demands the unused extern's Expand/Define/DeriveStaticCallees.
- DeriveInputDemand(+) -> forwarded_inputs (keying.rs:624-661) re-walks every clause itself and blocks on InputDemand of every extern named there.

Consumers of whole-body static edges: call-graph components / Recursive (keying.rs:219-272, 1093-1117), input-demand forwarding (ForwardingWalk, keying.rs:427-578), transport's statically_reaches (transport.rs:2215-2237).

Design constraint (the open question): clause reachability is only known per activation (ActivationAnalysis.entry_reachability), after AnalyzeActivation, and AnalyzeActivation needs InputDemand, which today is a whole-function summary built before any activation exists. Filtering edges by reachable clauses inverts that order.

Investigate on paper before a design, then write a proposal page.
Done when: 00420 and `1 + 2` run no job for an unreached function, and every work pin that moves drops.
title: Nothing unused creates work: a static edge exists only from a clause dispatch can select
